solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Quiet lanes meandering one after another (10)

indicators.note: lanes that meander wander about, so their letters wander into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A peaceful country walk along winding lanes, taken one after another.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is the whole opening phrase, and the letters happen to include the Q and U the answer needs side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: Things that are sequential come one after another in order.

clue.text: Cereal’s over by sink (4)

indicators.note: one piece sits next to the other

blocks.note: to sag is to sink or droop
O is the scorecard abbreviation for an over in cricket

annotation.surface: Breakfast cereal left out by the kitchen sink.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads the pieces back to front: O is 'by' SAG, and the answer puts SAG first.
annotation.definitionFit: Sago is a starchy grain-like food from palm pith, loosely classed as a cereal.

clue.text: Lacking ecstasy, supply crack (4)

indicators.note: the word goes without the letter named

blocks.note: to equip is to supply
E is slang for the drug ecstasy; it is removed

annotation.surface: Someone who, without their ecstasy, has to supply crack instead: a drug dealer's shortage.
annotation.walkthrough: The drug-trade surface is a disguise: 'crack' here is a joke or witty remark.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the informal sense: a crack, short for wisecrack, is a witty remark.

clue.text: Bold board perhaps using leverage (12)

blocks.note: boarding a ship or train is one way of entering it, hence 'perhaps'
prising something open is forcing it with a lever

annotation.surface: A daring move on a company board, applying pressure to get one's way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like the directors of a company, and 'leverage' like financial muscle; both are physical here.
annotation.definitionFit: An enterprising person is bold and willing to take on new ventures.

clue.text: Bones of seafarers found on island (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece is placed on top of the next

blocks.note: tars are sailors
I is the map abbreviation for island

annotation.surface: Sailors' skeletons discovered on a desert island.
annotation.walkthrough: TARS is a crossword favourite for sailors, alongside AB and SALT.
annotation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the small bones of the ankle, plural of tarsus.

clue.text: Person mechanically moving gold and red fruit before noon (9)

indicators.note: the pieces come ahead of the final N

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a tomato is a red fruit
N is the abbreviation for noon

annotation.surface: Someone sluggishly shifting gold and tomatoes about before lunch.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition spans three words: an automaton is a person who moves mechanically, like a robot.
annotation.definitionFit: Figuratively, an automaton is a person acting mechanically without thought.

clue.text: Sons pitch compasses and ruler (4)

indicators.note: to compass something is to surround it

blocks.note: pitch is a black tarry substance
S is the abbreviation for son, here plural sons

annotation.surface: A geometry set: the pupils pack their compasses and a ruler.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Compasses and ruler' reads as drawing instruments; compasses is the container verb and ruler the monarch.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the tsars were the emperors who ruled Russia until 1917.

clue.text: Temperature dropped when working clay-pit site in field (10)

indicators.note: the letter for temperature is left out
the remaining letters are put to work in a new order

blocks.note: the raw letters
T is the abbreviation for temperature; one T is removed

annotation.surface: An archaeological or geological report: the temperature fell while digging at a clay pit in a field.
annotation.walkthrough: Only one of the two Ts in CLAY-PIT SITE is dropped; the other stays in the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the area of work or study a person concentrates on can be called either.

clue.text: Muscle’s cramped by lazing about (10)

indicators.note: the muscle is squeezed inside the other word

blocks.note: lazing about is resting
a pec is a chest muscle (pectoral)

annotation.surface: A muscle seizes up from lying around idly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lazing about' looks like one phrase, but 'about' is the definition, meaning 'concerning'. The 's is just 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Respecting means concerning or regarding, just as 'about' does.

clue.text: Refuse to get drawn in by current flap about rich and famous (10)

indicators.note: the rubbish is pulled inside the other letters
I and TAG are turned round

blocks.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
a tag is a loose flap or tab
litter is refuse or rubbish

annotation.surface: A celebrity refuses to be dragged into a current fuss about the wealthy and famous.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' is a noun (rubbish), not a verb, and 'flap' is a tag rather than a panic.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a blend of glitter and literati, naming the fashionable celebrity set.

clue.text: Heavenly influencer’s famous channel retired (4)

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the word goes back to front

blocks.note: the Suez Canal is a famous shipping channel in Egypt

annotation.surface: A social-media influencer's well-known channel has been shut down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Influencer' and 'channel' suggest YouTube; the channel is a canal, and Zeus is a god with heavenly influence.
annotation.definitionFit: Zeus, king of the Greek gods, ruled the heavens and influenced events from there.

clue.text: Failing general hospital shown up after sick beset by pains (8,4)

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' turns the letters upward, back to front
this piece follows the first
the sick word is surrounded by the pains

blocks.note: aches are pains
ill means sick
Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

annotation.surface: A failing general hospital is exposed, overwhelmed by sickness and pain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Failing' looks like an adjective describing the hospital, but it is the noun: a weakness.
annotation.definitionFit: An Achilles heel is a single fatal weakness, a failing.

clue.text: Penalty scored by Rugby International changed match? You can bet on it (5,7)

indicators.note: the penalty is cut through by the other pieces, which sit inside it
the letters of the match are rearranged

blocks.note: a fine is a penalty
RU is short for Rugby Union
I is the abbreviation for international
MATCH rearranged

annotation.surface: A penalty kick scored in a rugby international turns the game; gamblers take note.
annotation.walkthrough: A fruit machine is the British name for a slot machine. 'Scored' means cut through, not a point won.
annotation.definitionFit: A fruit machine is a slot machine, something you literally put a bet into.

clue.text: One covering binding request to turn papers over is bound to succeed (5-5)

indicators.note: I and ROOF tie up the reversed letters between them
PTO and ID are turned over, back to front

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
PTO, please turn over, the note at the foot of a page
ID is identity papers
a roof is a covering

annotation.surface: A bookbinder's instruction to turn the pages over is sure to work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Binding' and 'papers' suggest bookbinding; binding is the container instruction, with I in front and ROOF behind.
annotation.definitionFit: Something idiot-proof cannot fail, however clumsily it is used.

clue.text: Dig outside channel topped by earth — an overlay of just one foot (10)

definitions.text: an overlay of just one foot

indicators.note: in a down clue, E sits at the top
the digging word goes around the channel

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for earth
to spade is to dig
a rill is a small stream or channel

annotation.surface: Instructions for laying a drain: dig round a channel, top with soil, one foot of cover.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a single shoe covers just one foot. 'One foot' sounds like a measurement of soil depth.
annotation.definitionFit: An espadrille is a canvas shoe, and one shoe is an overlay for a single foot.

clue.text: Slate counter, perhaps with wine beside it (9)

indicators.note: the pieces sit next to each other

blocks.note: a counter in a board game is one kind of disc
red is wine
used as it stands

annotation.surface: A slate kitchen counter with a bottle of wine standing next to it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slate' looks like the stone, but it is the verb: to criticise harshly.
annotation.definitionFit: To slate someone is to attack their reputation, to discredit them.

clue.text: Rambling Liberal used to lie about rival party member (9)

indicators.note: L and USED are laid down back to front

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
used as it stands
a Tory is a Conservative, rivals of the Liberals

annotation.surface: A long-winded Liberal politician used to tell lies about an opponent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Used to lie' reads as a past habit; the split is 'used' plus 'to lie about', the reversal instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Desultory means rambling, going from one thing to another without purpose.

clue.text: Firth and Grant beyond popular (5)

indicators.note: this piece comes after the other

blocks.note: something in is popular
to let is to grant or allow

annotation.surface: Colin Firth and Hugh Grant, two actors whose fame goes beyond ordinary popularity.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals make Firth and Grant look like the actors; a firth is a Scottish sea inlet, and grant is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A firth is a Scottish estuary or arm of the sea, an inlet.

clue.text: Sanctions precluding tons of Hungarian wines (5)

indicators.note: the wines shut out the letter for tons

blocks.note: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian wine
T is the abbreviation for ton; it is removed

annotation.surface: Trade sanctions keep tonnes of Hungarian wine out of the market.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sanctions' looks like the noun for penalties, but it is the verb meaning approves.
annotation.definitionFit: To sanction something is to approve it, and so it okays it.

clue.text: Confess and reveal unique diamond in one’s hand? (9)

blocks.note: to sing is to confess to the police
to let on is to reveal

annotation.surface: A plea to own up and show off the single precious diamond one is holding.
annotation.walkthrough: The diamond is a playing card: a singleton is the only card of a suit in a hand at bridge.
annotation.definitionFit: A singleton is a lone card of its suit, such as a single diamond in one's hand.

clue.text: Head explorer’s meaning to spend time in North Pole base (12)

indicators.note: the letter for time is used up and gone
what is left goes inside the other letters
a base version of North Pole is corrupted, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: NORTH POLE rearranged
the gist is the meaning
T is the abbreviation for time; it is removed from GIST

annotation.surface: A polar explorer's leader means to pass a season at the North Pole base camp.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head explorer' looks like an expedition leader; a phrenologist studied the bumps on people's heads.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrenologist examined the shape of the skull to read character, literally exploring heads.

clue.text: Raised grievance on the radio (5)

indicators.note: heard over the airwaves rather than read

blocks.note: a groan is a complaint

annotation.surface: A complaint voiced on a radio phone-in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raised' looks like a complaint being raised, tying it to 'grievance'; it is the past participle meaning cultivated.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as past participles: crops are raised or grown by a farmer.

clue.text: Swerve erratically to some extent? (4)

indicators.note: only part of the words is used

blocks.note: hidden across the two words: swerVE ERratically

annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: to veer is, in part, to swerve erratically.
annotation.definitionFit: To veer is to swerve or change direction suddenly.

clue.text: Rum could be what leads to rows in theatre bar area (4)

indicators.note: to bar is to exclude, so the A is kept out

blocks.clueFragment: what leads to rows in theatre
blocks.note: in a theatre you walk down the aisle to reach your row
A is the abbreviation for area; it is removed

annotation.surface: Rum being served in the theatre bar, reached past the rows of seats.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rum' and 'theatre bar' suggest a drink; Rum is a small island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides.
annotation.definitionFit: Rum is an island in the Hebrides, so it could be described as an isle.

clue.text: Shamelessly look at withdrawing hotel goody bags (4)

indicators.note: the letters draw back, reading right to left
the phrase holds the answer inside it

blocks.note: the letters inside hotEL GOody

annotation.surface: Someone brazenly eyeing the goody bags as they leave a hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bags' looks like the noun after 'goody'; it is a verb meaning holds.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, with 'shamelessly' carrying the leering, lecherous flavour of the word.

clue.text: Humour in function hosted by enviable neighbours moving east (10)

indicators.note: the function is a guest inside the neighbours
one letter of the neighbours shifts position

blocks.note: the neighbours everyone tries to keep up with
E for east; the second E of JONESES moves up to just after JO, giving JOENESS
cos, short for cosine, a trigonometric function

annotation.surface: Finding the humour in a party thrown by the envied neighbours who are moving house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Keeping up with the Joneses' means trying to match the neighbours' lifestyle, hence enviable. 'Function' is the maths kind, not a party.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a rare noun from jocose, meaning given to joking.

clue.text: Vote against large ironclad contract (4)

indicators.note: one piece is placed next to the other
the iron letters clad, or wrap, the L

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
L is the abbreviation for large
a voter marks the ballot with an X

annotation.surface: Voting against a big watertight contract.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ironclad contract' reads as an unbreakable agreement; 'contract' is the verb, as a muscle does, and 'ironclad' splits into iron plus clad.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym from the gym: flexing a muscle tightens and shortens it.

clue.text: In general rage, irritated after new drills failed badly (2,3,5)

indicators.note: the rage is stirred up into a new order
this piece follows the first
N bores into the other letters
the letters of badly break down into a new order

blocks.note: BADLY rearranged
N is the abbreviation for new
RAGE rearranged

annotation.surface: Widespread fury, made worse after the new training exercises went badly wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In general' opens the clue as if it meant 'widespread'; it is the definition. 'Drills' is the container verb, not training.
annotation.definitionFit: By and large means generally, on the whole.
